NKJV.1: And Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, except at my word.”
NKJV.2: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
NKJV.3: “Get away from here and turn eastward, and hide by the Brook Cherith, which flows into the Jordan.
NKJV.4: And it will be that you shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
NKJV.5: So he went and did according to the word of the LORD, for he went and stayed by the Brook Cherith, which flows into the Jordan.
NKJV.6: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.
NKJV.7: And it happened after a while that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
NKJV.8: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
NKJV.9: “Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. See, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
NKJV.10: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, indeed a widow was there gathering sticks. And he called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup, that I may drink.”
NKJV.11: And as she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”
NKJV.12: So she said, “As the LORD your God lives, I do not have bread, only a handful of flour in a bin, and a little oil in a jar; and see, I am gathering a couple of sticks that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat it, and die.”
NKJV.13: And Elijah said to her, “Do not fear; go and do as you have said, but make me a small cake from it first, and bring it to me; and afterward make some for yourself and your son.
NKJV.14: For thus says the LORD God of Israel: ‘The bin of flour shall not be used up, nor shall the jar of oil run dry, until the day the LORD sends rain on the earth.’ ”
NKJV.15: So she went away and did according to the word of Elijah; and she and he and her household ate for many days.
NKJV.16: The bin of flour was not used up, nor did the jar of oil run dry, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke by Elijah.
NKJV.17: Now it happened after these things that the son of the woman who owned the house became sick. And his sickness was so serious that there was no breath left in him.
NKJV.18: So she said to Elijah, “What have I to do with you, O man of God? Have you come to me to bring my sin to remembrance, and to kill my son?”
NKJV.19: And he said to her, “Give me your son.” So he took him out of her arms and carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
NKJV.20: Then he cried out to the LORD and said, “O LORD my God, have You also brought tragedy on the widow with whom I lodge, by killing her son?”
NKJV.21: And he stretched himself out on the child three times, and cried out to the LORD and said, “O LORD my God, I pray, let this child’s soul come back to him.”
NKJV.22: Then the LORD heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came back to him, and he revived.
NKJV.23: And Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. And Elijah said, “See, your son lives!”
NKJV.24: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now by this I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is the truth.”

ESV.1: Now Elijah the Tishbite, of Tishbe  in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word.”
ESV.2: And the word of the LORD came to him:
ESV.3: “Depart from here and turn eastward and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
ESV.4: You shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
ESV.5: So he went and did according to the word of the LORD. He went and lived by the brook Cherith that is east of the Jordan.
ESV.6: And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the brook.
ESV.7: And after a while the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
ESV.8: Then the word of the LORD came to him,
ESV.9: “Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to feed you.”
ESV.10: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks. And he called to her and said, “Bring me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.”
ESV.11: And as she was going to bring it, he called to her and said, “Bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”
ESV.12: And she said, “As the LORD your God lives, I have nothing baked, only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. And now I am gathering a couple of sticks that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die.”
ESV.13: And Elijah said to her, “Do not fear; go and do as you have said. But first make me a little cake of it and bring it to me, and afterward make something for yourself and your son.
ESV.14: For thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, ‘The jar of flour shall not be spent, and the jug of oil shall not be empty, until the day that the LORD sends rain upon the earth.’”
ESV.15: And she went and did as Elijah said. And she and he and her household ate for many days.
ESV.16: The jar of flour was not spent, neither did the jug of oil become empty, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by Elijah.
ESV.17: After this the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill. And his illness was so severe that there was no breath left in him.
ESV.18: And she said to Elijah, “What have you against me, O man of God? You have come to me to bring my sin to remembrance and to cause the death of my son!”
ESV.19: And he said to her, “Give me your son.” And he took him from her arms and carried him up into the upper chamber where he lodged, and laid him on his own bed.
ESV.20: And he cried to the LORD, “O LORD my God, have you brought calamity even upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by killing her son?”
ESV.21: Then he stretched himself upon the child three times and cried to the LORD, “O LORD my God, let this child's life  come into him again.”
ESV.22: And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah. And the life of the child came into him again, and he revived.
ESV.23: And Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper chamber into the house and delivered him to his mother. And Elijah said, “See, your son lives.”
ESV.24: And the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.”

NASB.1: Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, 'As the LORD, the God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, surely there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word.'
NASB.2: The word of the LORD came to him, saying,
NASB.3: 'Go away from here and turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
NASB.4: 'It shall be that you will drink of the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to provide for you there.'
NASB.5: So he went and did according to the word of the LORD, for he went and lived by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
NASB.6: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he would drink from the brook.
NASB.7: It happened after a while that the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
NASB.8: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
NASB.9: 'Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there; behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.'
NASB.10: So he arose and went to Zarephath, and when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks; and he called to her and said, 'Please get me a little water in a jar, that I may drink.'
NASB.11: As she was going to get [it], he called to her and said, 'Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand.'
NASB.12: But she said, 'As the LORD your God lives, I have no bread, only a handful of flour in the bowl and a little oil in the jar; and behold, I am gathering a few sticks that I may go in and prepare for me and my son, that we may eat it and die.'
NASB.13: Then Elijah said to her, 'Do not fear; go, do as you have said, but make me a little bread cake from it first and bring [it] out to me, and afterward you may make [one] for yourself and for your son.
NASB.14: 'For thus says the LORD God of Israel, 'The bowl of flour shall not be exhausted, nor shall the jar of oil be empty, until the day that the LORD sends rain on the face of the earth.''
NASB.15: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and she and he and her household ate for [many] days.
NASB.16: The bowl of flour was not exhausted nor did the jar of oil become empty, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke through Elijah.
NASB.17: Now it came about after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick; and his sickness was so severe that there was no breath left in him.
NASB.18: So she said to Elijah, 'What do I have to do with you, O man of God? You have come to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance and to put my son to death!'
NASB.19: He said to her, 'Give me your son.' Then he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper room where he was living, and laid him on his own bed.
NASB.20: He called to the LORD and said, 'O LORD my God, have You also brought calamity to the widow with whom I am staying, by causing her son to die?'
NASB.21: Then he stretched himself upon the child three times, and called to the LORD and said, 'O LORD my God, I pray You, let this child's life return to him.'
NASB.22: The LORD heard the voice of Elijah, and the life of the child returned to him and he revived.
NASB.23: Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother; and Elijah said, 'See, your son is alive.'
NASB.24: Then the woman said to Elijah, 'Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.'

WEB.1: Elijah the Tishbite, who was one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As Yahweh, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.”
WEB.2: Then Yahweh’s word came to him, saying,
WEB.3: “Go away from here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan.
WEB.4: You shall drink from the brook. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
WEB.5: So he went and did according to Yahweh’s word; for he went and lived by the brook Cherith that is before the Jordan.
WEB.6: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.
WEB.7: After a while, the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
WEB.8: Yahweh’s word came to him, saying,
WEB.9: “Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to sustain you.”
WEB.10: So he arose and went to Zarephath; and when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called to her, and said, “Please get me a little water in a jar, that I may drink.”
WEB.11: As she was going to get it, he called to her, and said, “Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”
WEB.12: She said, “As Yahweh your God lives, I don’t have a cake, but a handful of meal in a jar, and a little oil in a jar. Behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.”
WEB.13: Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you have said; but make me a little cake from it first, and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for you and for your son.
WEB.14: For Yahweh, the God of Israel says, ‘The jar of meal will not run out, and the jar of oil will not fail, until the day that Yahweh sends rain on the earth.’”
WEB.15: She went and did according to the saying of Elijah; and she, and he, and her house, ate many days.
WEB.16: The jar of meal didn’t run out, and the jar of oil did not fail, according to Yahweh’s word, which he spoke by Elijah.
WEB.17: After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick; and his sickness was so severe that there was no breath left in him.
WEB.18: She said to Elijah, “What have I to do with you, you man of God? You have come to me to bring my sin to memory, and to kill my son!”
WEB.19: He said to her, “Give me your son.” He took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into the room where he stayed, and laid him on his own bed.
WEB.20: He cried to Yahweh, and said, “Yahweh my God, have you also brought evil on the widow with whom I am staying, by killing her son?”
WEB.21: He stretched himself on the child three times, and cried to Yahweh, and said, “Yahweh my God, please let this child’s soul come into him again.”
WEB.22: Yahweh listened to the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
WEB.23: Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the room into the house, and delivered him to his mother; and Elijah said, “Behold, your son lives.”
WEB.24: The woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that Yahweh’s word in your mouth is truth.”

AMP.2: And the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
AMP.3: "Go from here and turn eastward and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan [River].
AMP.4: You shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to sustain you there [with food]."
AMP.5: So he went and did in accordance with the word of the LORD; he went and lived by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
AMP.6: And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he would drink from the brook.
AMP.7: It happened after a while that the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
AMP.8: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
AMP.9: "Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you."
AMP.10: So he set out and went to Zarephath, and when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks [for firewood]. He called out to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a jar, so that I may drink."
AMP.11: As she was going to get it, he called to her and said, "Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand."
AMP.12: But she said, "As the LORD your God lives, I have no bread, only a handful of flour in the bowl and a little oil in the jar. See, I am gathering a few sticks so that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it [as our last meal] and die."
AMP.13: Elijah said to her, "Do not fear; go and do as you have said. Just make me a little bread from it first and bring it out to me, and afterward you may make one for yourself and for your son.
AMP.14: For this is what the LORD God of Israel says: 'The bowl of flour shall not be exhausted nor shall the jar of oil be empty until the day that the LORD sends rain [again] on the face of the earth.'"
AMP.15: She went and did as Elijah said. And she and he and her household ate for many days.
AMP.16: The bowl of flour was not exhausted nor did the jar of oil become empty, in accordance the word of the LORD which He spoke through Elijah.
AMP.17: It happened after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick; and his illness was so severe that there was no breath left in him.
AMP.18: So she said to Elijah, "What [problem] is there between you and me, O man of God? Have you come to me to bring my sin to mind and to put my son to death?"
AMP.19: He said to her, "Give me your son." Then he took him from her arms and carried him up to the upper room where he was living, and laid him on his own bed.
AMP.20: He called to the LORD and said, "O LORD my God, have You brought further tragedy to the widow with whom I am staying, by causing her son to die?"
AMP.21: Then he stretched himself out upon the child three times, and called to the LORD and said, "O LORD my God, please let this child's life return to him."
AMP.22: The LORD heard the voice of Elijah, and the life of the child returned to him and he revived.
AMP.23: Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the [lower part of the] house and gave him to his mother; and Elijah said, "See, your son is alive."
AMP.24: Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth."

CSB17.1: Now Elijah <sup>ⓜ</sup> the Tishbite, from the Gilead settlers, <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup> said to Ahab, “As the LORD God of Israel lives, <sup>ⓐ</sup> in whose presence I stand, there will be no dew or rain during these years except by my command!” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.2: Then the word of the LORD came to him:
CSB17.3: “Leave here, turn eastward, and hide <sup>ⓒ</sup> at the Wadi Cherith where it enters the Jordan.
CSB17.4: You are to drink from the wadi. I have commanded the ravens <sup>ⓓ</sup> to provide for you there.”
CSB17.5: So he proceeded to do what the LORD commanded. Elijah left and lived at the Wadi Cherith where it enters the Jordan.
CSB17.6: The ravens kept bringing him bread and meat in the morning and in the evening, <sup>ⓔ</sup> and he would drink from the wadi.
CSB17.7: After a while, the wadi dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
CSB17.8: Then the word of the LORD came to him:
CSB17.9: “Get up, go to Zarephath <sup>ⓕ</sup> that belongs to Sidon and stay there. Look, I have commanded a woman who is a widow to provide for you there.”
CSB17.10: So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the city gate, there was a widow gathering wood. Elijah called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup and let me drink.” <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.11: As she went to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand.”
CSB17.12: But she said, “As the LORD your God lives, <sup>ⓗ</sup> I don’t have anything baked — only a handful of flour in the jar and a bit of oil <sup>ⓘ</sup> in the jug. Just now, I am gathering a couple of sticks in order to go prepare it for myself and my son so we can eat it and die.” <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.13: Then Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid; go and do as you have said. But first make me a small loaf from it and bring it out to me. Afterward, you may make some for yourself and your son,
CSB17.14: for this is what the LORD God of Israel says, ‘The flour jar will not become empty and the oil jug will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain on the surface of the land.’” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.15: So she proceeded to do according to the word of Elijah. Then the woman, Elijah, and her household ate for many days. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.16: The flour jar did not become empty, and the oil jug did not run dry, according to the word of the LORD he had spoken through <sup>[2]</sup> Elijah.
CSB17.17: After this, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. His illness got worse until he stopped breathing. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.18: She said to Elijah, “Man of God, <sup>ⓝ</sup> why are you here? <sup>ⓐ</sup> Have you come to call attention to my iniquity <sup>ⓑ</sup> so that my son is put to death?”
CSB17.19: But Elijah said to her, “Give me your son.” So he took him from her arms, brought him up to the upstairs room <sup>ⓒ</sup> where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
CSB17.20: Then he cried out to the LORD <sup>ⓓ</sup> and said, “LORD my God, have you also brought tragedy on the widow I am staying with by killing her son?”
CSB17.21: Then he stretched himself out over the boy three times. <sup>ⓔ</sup> He cried out to the LORD and said, “LORD my God, please let this boy’s life come into him again!”
CSB17.22: So the LORD listened to Elijah, and the boy’s life came into him again, and he lived. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.23: Then Elijah took the boy, brought him down from the upstairs room into the house, and gave him to his mother. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Elijah said, “Look, your son is alive.”
CSB17.24: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know you are a man of God <sup>ⓗ</sup> and the LORD’s word from your mouth is true.” <sup>ⓘ</sup>

NLT.1: Now Elijah, who was from Tishbe in Gilead, told King Ahab, “As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives — the God I serve — there will be no dew or rain during the next few years until I give the word!”
NLT.2: Then the LORD said to Elijah,
NLT.3: “Go to the east and hide by Kerith Brook, near where it enters the Jordan River.
NLT.4: Drink from the brook and eat what the ravens bring you, for I have commanded them to bring you food.”
NLT.5: So Elijah did as the LORD told him and camped beside Kerith Brook, east of the Jordan.
NLT.6: The ravens brought him bread and meat each morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.
NLT.7: But after a while the brook dried up, for there was no rainfall anywhere in the land.
NLT.8: Then the LORD said to Elijah,
NLT.9: “Go and live in the village of Zarephath, near the city of Sidon. I have instructed a widow there to feed you.”
NLT.10: So he went to Zarephath. As he arrived at the gates of the village, he saw a widow gathering sticks, and he asked her, “Would you please bring me a little water in a cup?”
NLT.11: As she was going to get it, he called to her, “Bring me a bite of bread, too.”
NLT.12: But she said, “I swear by the LORD your God that I don’t have a single piece of bread in the house. And I have only a handful of flour left in the jar and a little cooking oil in the bottom of the jug. I was just gathering a few sticks to cook this last meal, and then my son and I will die.”
NLT.13: But Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid! Go ahead and do just what you’ve said, but make a little bread for me first. Then use what’s left to prepare a meal for yourself and your son.
NLT.14: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There will always be flour and olive oil left in your containers until the time when the LORD sends rain and the crops grow again!”
NLT.15: So she did as Elijah said, and she and Elijah and her family continued to eat for many days.
NLT.16: There was always enough flour and olive oil left in the containers, just as the LORD had promised through Elijah.
NLT.17: Some time later the woman’s son became sick. He grew worse and worse, and finally he died.
NLT.18: Then she said to Elijah, “O man of God, what have you done to me? Have you come here to point out my sins and kill my son?”
NLT.19: But Elijah replied, “Give me your son.” And he took the child’s body from her arms, carried him up the stairs to the room where he was staying, and laid the body on his bed.
NLT.20: Then Elijah cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, why have you brought tragedy to this widow who has opened her home to me, causing her son to die?”
NLT.21: And he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, please let this child’s life return to him.”
NLT.22: The LORD heard Elijah’s prayer, and the life of the child returned, and he revived!
NLT.23: Then Elijah brought him down from the upper room and gave him to his mother. “Look!” he said. “Your son is alive!”
NLT.24: Then the woman told Elijah, “Now I know for sure that you are a man of God, and that the LORD truly speaks through you.”

MSG.1: And then this happened: Elijah the Tishbite, from among the settlers of Gilead, confronted Ahab: "As surely as God lives, the God of Israel before whom I stand in obedient service, the next years are going to see a total drought—not a drop of dew or rain unless I say otherwise."
MSG.3: "Get out of here, and fast. Head east and hide out at the Kerith Ravine on the other side of the Jordan River.
MSG.4: You can drink fresh water from the brook; I've ordered the ravens to feed you."
MSG.5: Elijah obeyed God's orders. He went and camped in the Kerith canyon on the other side of the Jordan.
MSG.6: And sure enough, ravens brought him his meals, both breakfast and supper, and he drank from the brook.
MSG.7: Eventually the brook dried up because of the drought.
MSG.9: "Get up and go to Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've instructed a woman who lives there, a widow, to feed you."
MSG.10: So he got up and went to Zarephath. As he came to the entrance of the village he met a woman, a widow, gathering firewood. He asked her, "Please, would you bring me a little water in a jug? I need a drink."
MSG.11: As she went to get it, he called out, "And while you're at it, would you bring me something to eat?"
MSG.12: She said, "I swear, as surely as your God lives, I don't have so much as a biscuit. I have a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a bottle; you found me scratching together just enough firewood to make a last meal for my son and me. After we eat it, we'll die."
MSG.13: Elijah said to her, "Don't worry about a thing. Go ahead and do what you've said. But first make a small biscuit for me and bring it back here. Then go ahead and make a meal from what's left for you and your son.
MSG.14: This is the word of the God of Israel: 'The jar of flour will not run out and the bottle of oil will not become empty before God sends rain on the land and ends this drought.' "
MSG.15: And she went right off and did it, did just as Elijah asked. And it turned out as he said—daily food for her and her family.
MSG.16: The jar of meal didn't run out and the bottle of oil didn't become empty: God's promise fulfilled to the letter, exactly as Elijah had delivered it!
MSG.17: Later on the woman's son became sick. The sickness took a turn for the worse—and then he stopped breathing.
MSG.18: The woman said to Elijah, "Why did you ever show up here in the first place—a holy man barging in, exposing my sins, and killing my son?"
MSG.19:
Elijah said, "Hand me your son."
He then took him from her bosom, carried him up to the loft where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
MSG.20: Then he prayed, "O God, my God, why have you brought this terrible thing on this widow who has opened her home to me? Why have you killed her son?"
MSG.21: Three times he stretched himself out full-length on the boy, praying with all his might, "God, my God, put breath back into this boy's body!"
MSG.22: God listened to Elijah's prayer and put breath back into his body—he was alive!
MSG.23: Elijah picked the boy up, carried him downstairs from the loft, and gave him to his mother. "Here's your son," said Elijah, "alive!"
MSG.24: The woman said to Elijah, "I see it all now—you are a holy man. When you speak, God speaks—a true word!"

NIV.1:
Elijah Fed by Ravens
Now Elijah the Tishbite, from Tishbe in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of Israel, lives, whom I serve, there will be neither dew nor rain in the next few years except at my word.”
NIV.2: Then the word of the Lord came to Elijah:
NIV.3: “Leave here, turn eastward and hide in the Kerith Ravine, east of the Jordan.
NIV.4: You will drink from the brook, and I have ordered the ravens to feed you there.”
NIV.5: So he did what the Lord had told him. He went to the Kerith Ravine, east of the Jordan, and stayed there.
NIV.6: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the brook.
NIV.7:
The Widow at Zarephath
Some time later the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
NIV.8: Then the word of the Lord came to him:
NIV.9: “Go at once to Zarephath of Sidon and stay there. I have commanded a widow in that place to supply you with food.”
NIV.10: So he went to Zarephath. When he came to the town gate, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called to her and asked, “Would you bring me a little water in a jar so I may have a drink?”
NIV.11: As she was going to get it, he called, “And bring me, please, a piece of bread.”
NIV.12: “As surely as the Lord your God lives,” she replied, “I don’t have any bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a few sticks to take home and make a meal for myself and my son, that we may eat it—and die.”
NIV.13: Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go home and do as you have said. But first make a small cake of bread for me from what you have and bring it to me, and then make something for yourself and your son.
NIV.14: For this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘The jar of flour will not be used up and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the Lord gives rain on the land.’”
NIV.15: She went away and did as Elijah had told her. So there was food every day for Elijah and for the woman and her family.
NIV.16: For the jar of flour was not used up and the jug of oil did not run dry, in keeping with the word of the Lord spoken by Elijah.
NIV.17: Some time later the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. He grew worse and worse, and finally stopped breathing.
NIV.18: She said to Elijah, “What do you have against me, man of God? Did you come to remind me of my sin and kill my son?”
NIV.19: “Give me your son,” Elijah replied. He took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
NIV.20: Then he cried out to the Lord, “O Lord my God, have you brought tragedy also upon this widow I am staying with, by causing her son to die?”
NIV.21: Then he stretched himself out on the boy three times and cried to the Lord, “O Lord my God, let this boy’s life return to him!”
NIV.22: The Lord heard Elijah’s cry, and the boy’s life returned to him, and he lived.
NIV.23: Elijah picked up the child and carried him down from the room into the house. He gave him to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive!”
NIV.24: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the Lord from your mouth is the truth.”

NET.1: Elijah the Tishbite, from Tishbe in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As certainly as the LORD God of Israel lives (whom I serve), there will be no dew or rain in the years ahead unless I give the command.”
NET.3: “Leave here and travel eastward. Hide out in the Kerith Valley near the Jordan.
NET.4: Drink from the stream; I have already told the ravens to bring you food there.”
NET.5: So he did as the LORD told him; he went and lived in the Kerith Valley near the Jordan.
NET.6: The ravens would bring him bread and meat each morning and evening, and he would drink from the stream.
NET.7: After a while, the stream dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
NET.9: “Get up, go to Zarephath in Sidonian territory, and live there. I have already told a widow who lives there to provide for you.”
NET.10: So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he went through the city gate, there was a widow gathering wood. He called out to her, “Please give me a cup of water, so I can take a drink.”
NET.11: As she went to get it, he called out to her, “Please bring me a piece of bread.”
NET.12: She said, “As certainly as the LORD your God lives, I have no food, except for a handful of flour in a jar and a little olive oil in a jug. Right now I am gathering a couple of sticks for a fire. Then I’m going home to make one final meal for my son and myself. After we have eaten that, we will die of starvation.”
NET.13: Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you planned. But first make a small cake for me and bring it to me; then make something for yourself and your son.
NET.14: For this is what the LORD God of Israel says, ‘The jar of flour will not be empty and the jug of oil will not run out until the day the LORD makes it rain on the surface of the ground.’”
NET.15: She went and did as Elijah told her; there was always enough food for Elijah and for her and her family.
NET.16: The jar of flour was never empty and the jug of oil never ran out, just as the LORD had promised through Elijah.
NET.17: After this the son of the woman who owned the house got sick. His illness was so severe he could no longer breathe.
NET.18: She asked Elijah, “Why, prophet, have you come to me to confront me with my sin and kill my son?”
NET.19: He said to her, “Hand me your son.” He took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him down on his bed.
NET.20: Then he called out to the LORD, “O LORD, my God, are you also bringing disaster on this widow I am staying with by killing her son?”
NET.21: He stretched out over the boy three times and called out to the LORD, “O LORD, my God, please let this boy’s breath return to him.”
NET.22: The LORD answered Elijah’s prayer; the boy’s breath returned to him and he lived.
NET.23: Elijah took the boy, brought him down from the upper room to the house, and handed him to his mother. Elijah then said, “See, your son is alive!”
NET.24: The woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a prophet and that the LORD really does speak through you.”
